newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund vol rises, BTP vol dips on EU summit.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund vol rises, BTP vol dips on EU summit.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bunds and BTPs diverged on Tuesday, as investors sold mark assets in favour of buying BTPs, traders in London said.
Traders said the fall in underlying Bund futures had been sparked by concerns that it was overvalued, particularly as the September Bund future hit a new contract high of 101.88 earlier on Tuesday.
Although Italian BTPs also hit a new high, traders said the Italian market still has potential to outperform.
"Bunds seem to be headed for a larger correction," said a broker at a French house on the LIFFE floor. "There's also a bit of 'buy the rumour, sell the fact' over the Amsterdam summit going on."
European Union leaders in Amsterdam are in the last stages of their meeting, trying to agree a new treaty.
Traders said the market was not expecting any further problems, and a single European currency appeared to be back on track for a start date of 1999.
September Bunds were down 0.33 at 101.36, while September BTPs were up 0.21 at 132.39.
September Bund option volatility was at 5.85 percent, up from 5.5 percent on Monday, and September BTP option volatility fell to 7.75 percent from 7.85 percent.
A trader at a British brokerage said buying of September Bund puts was brisk, with 99.50 and 97.00 strikes popular.
In BTPs, trade was more limited on the floor, although OTC trades were relatively active.
